newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria LNG says committed to $4 bln gas project.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria LNG says committed to $4 bln gas project.

text.p: Nigerian LNG Limited (NLNG), which is handling the country's $4 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) project, on Tuesday denied local media reports of problems with the scheme.
"The company and its management remain fully committed to the successful completion of the LNG project," it said in a statement.

Last month the chief executive of the NLNG Limited, Steve Ollereanshaw told journalists on tour of the project site in Bonny Island in the southeast that it was slightly ahead of schedule and was 40 percent completed.
But two weeks later oil minister Dan Etete unceremoniously sacked the board of directors of the company and said the management would now report directly to the oil ministry.
"The dissolution of the board lays to rest some unhealthy developments threatening the company's accountability," Etete's statement at the time without elaboration.
The weekly Newswatch magazine wrote in its latest edition on Monday that government's continued interference in the company would affect the execution of the project.

"The stage appears set for a confrontation between private investors in NLNG and the government over the later's frequent interferences in the project," said Newswatch in the report quoting unnamed officials of the company.

But the company statement retorted that: "Nigeria LNG Limited wishes to make it clear that it has made no statements to the press on this issue and denies the comments purportedly credited to its so-called officials."
The four shareholders in the project are state oil firm Nigerian National Petreoleum Corp, Shell Sas BV, Elf Aquitaine and Agip SpA.
They are financing it from their own funds and have placed $2.873 billion in escrow accounts to execute the project.
The oil ministry says LNG will be delivered in 1999 as scheduled.
An official of the company said Ollereanshaw was currently visiting the project site but added that the dissolution of the board of directors would have no effect on its execution.
The project has suffered a series of postponements in the past and frequent management changes but Nigeria's present military government has generally shown more commitment to it.
The project is to produce 7.5 billion cubic metres of gas annually for delivery to customers in Spain, France and Turkey.
The fourth and biggest buyer Enel of Italy terminated the contract in December and the issue is now before an arbitration panel in Switzerland.
Newswatch said the Enel issue appeared to be the immediate reason for the disolution of the board.
It said while Etete favoured reaching a settlement with Enel based on talks he had with the Italian government, the board had ignored him and pressed ahead with arbitration.
